title: Chronica
author: Sulpicius Severus
source: Translated by Claude from stoa0270.stoa001.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's CSEL.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
availability: CC BY-SA 4.0, as its source requires: credit Open Greek and Latin's CSEL and this AI translation, and share adaptations under the same licence.

passages.original: erat ea tempestate apud Babylonios Beli antiquissimi regis, cuius etiam Virgilius meminit, ex sere simulacrum, quod superstitione hominum consecratum Cyrus quoque adorare erat solitus, antistitum eius dolo illusus, qui uesci effigiem illam atque potare affirmabant, cum diurnam pensitationem, quae idolo inferebatur, clam ipsi absumerent.
passages.english: At that time there was among the Babylonians a bronze statue of Bel, a most ancient king, whom Virgil also mentions; it had been consecrated by the superstition of men, and Cyrus too was accustomed to worship it, deceived by the trickery of its priests, who claimed that the image ate and drank, when they themselves secretly consumed the daily allowance that was brought to the idol.
passages.notes: "ex sere" is evidently a scanning error for "ex aere" (of bronze).

passages.original: ceterum Arriani non hos potius quam Athanasium remouere cupiebant. itaque imperatorem eo usque compellunt, ut Athanasius exulatum ad Gallias mitteretur.
passages.english: But the Arians did not wish to remove these men so much as Athanasius. And so they pressed the emperor to the point that Athanasius was sent into exile to the Gauls.

passages.original: uerumtamen ea tempestate Arriani perfidiam suam occultabant: non ausi palam erroris sui dogmata praedicare catholicos se gerebant, nihil sibi prius agendum rati quam ut Athanasium ecclesia submouerent, qui semper eis uelut murus obstiterat: quo remoto reliquos in libidinem suam cessuros sperabant.
passages.english: Nevertheless at that time the Arians were concealing their faithlessness: not daring to preach the doctrines of their error openly, they conducted themselves as catholics, thinking that nothing should be done by them before they removed Athanasius from the church, who had always stood against them like a wall; once he was removed, they hoped that the rest would yield to their will.

passages.original: Osium quoque ab Hispania in eandem perfidiam concessisse opinio fuit: quod eo mirum atque incredibile uidetur, quia omni fere aetatis suae tempore constantissimus nostrarum partium. et Nicaena synodus auctore illo confecta habebatur: nisi fatiscente aeuo — etenim maior centenario fuit, ut sanctus Hilarius in epistolis refert — delirauerat.
passages.english: There was also a report that Ossius from Spain had gone over to the same faithlessness; this seems all the more astonishing and incredible because for almost the whole of his life he had been a most steadfast [member] of our party. And the Nicene synod was held to have been brought about on his initiative. [This could only be] unless, with his age failing (for he was over a hundred, as Saint Hilary reports in his letters), he had lost his wits.
passages.notes: "Osium" is Ossius (Hosius) of Córdoba. The "nisi" clause is elliptical; "[This could only be]" is supplied to carry the sense.
